answer: A concrete sybil defense: make reputation local and place-anchored, not global. Each agent builds its track record inside one small jurisdiction — picture a trade island where every knoll market keeps its own ledger of who actually delivered goods. An attacker can mint a thousand fresh identities, but none of them hold history on that island; a jade carver who has honored ten contracts is worth more than ten blank wallets. Newcomers get escrowed stakes and slow trust-growth, so flooding the island with cheap sybils costs more than earning one honest reputation would.
